title: Integration test fixtures insert public.tenant rows without tenant_type='test', so clean_test_db.py's tenant_type-filtered cleanup never removes them — leaked production-typed tenants accumulate across test runs and cause downstream failures (e.g. ISS-503 pre-flight LEGACY_RLS count)
notes:
Discovered while verifying the ISS-0099 fix (#355). migrations/GBL-080_env01_tenant_type_field.sql adds tenant.tenant_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'production'. Every INSERT INTO public.tenant across the majority of integration test files (helpers.zig's shared harness seed included) omits tenant_type, so every one of those rows is created as tenant_type='production'. tools/clean_test_db.py only deletes rows where tenant_type = 'test' (preserving slug='default'); production-typed disposable fixture tenants are never swept. Observed impact: after running the full test-integration-svc suite once, `SELECT tenant_type, storage_mode, count(*) FROM public.tenant GROUP BY 1,2` showed 15 leaked production/LEGACY_RLS rows; a subsequent migrations-related test (db_integration_test TC-DB-01-01/02) failed because an ISS-503 pre-flight check raised 'N tenant(s) still in LEGACY_RLS mode', counting these leaked fixture rows as real production tenants. Manually deleting the leaked rows (`DELETE FROM public.tenant WHERE tenant_type='production' AND slug != 'default'`) restored a clean baseline (74 pre-existing unrelated failures, confirmed identical before/after the ISS-0099 fix — see PR for #355). This is NOT introduced by the ISS-0099 fix; TC-SPT-01-06's own inserted row is self-cleaning via an unconditional defer regardless of tenant_type and does not require this fix.

WF-03 Step 0.5/1 diagnosis (2026-07-31, run WF03-iss0100-20260731, see docs/issue-reports/ISS-0100-diagnosis.yaml for full evidence): confirmed tools/clean_test_db.py ALREADY sweeps `tenant_type='production' AND slug != 'default'` rows (present since commit 106bb44, predating this issue) — verified live: 15 leaked LEGACY_RLS rows removed cleanly, zero FK errors. The remaining defect is TWO compounding causes, not a broken cleanup: (1) the fixture-insert bug as originally filed — bare `INSERT INTO tenant` statements across helpers.zig/svc01/svc04/adp07/adp04a/tenant_config_realm/oidc09-35 omit both tenant_type (defaults 'production' per GBL-080) and storage_mode (defaults 'LEGACY_RLS' per migrations/086_iss107_tenant_storage_mode.sql), so every one of these rows is exactly the shape GBL-084's guard counts; (2) migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql's pre-flight guard does NOT record itself as applied in schema_migrations when it fails (see its own header comment, lines 7-9), so tests/integration/helpers.zig TestHarness.init() -> Migrations.run() retries GBL-084 on EVERY test-binary startup until it first succeeds — meaning any leaked production/LEGACY_RLS row inserted earlier in the SAME `zig build` invocation (clean_test_db.py runs once at the start of the invocation, not between test binaries) causes every later TestHarness.init() call in that invocation, including db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01/02 (compiled into tests/integration/main_test.zig, part of the shared test-integration step), to re-fail the same guard. No narrower fixture/slug-collision bug found: grep confirms none of the leaking inserts use slug='default' or any other value clean_test_db.py's exclusion would accidentally protect.
candidate_resolution:
Either (a) tools/clean_test_db.py should also sweep production-typed tenants whose slug is not 'default' and not in an explicit allowlist of persistent seed tenants (e.g. by tracking which slugs the harness itself seeds vs which are ephemeral per-test), or (b) every test-fixture tenant INSERT (starting with helpers.zig's ensureDefaultOidcSeeds, which runs on every TestHarness.init()) should set tenant_type='test' with a production_tenant_id pointing at the default tenant to satisfy ck_tenant_type_fk_coherence. Option (b) is more correct long-term but touches 12+ files; needs its own WF-03/WF-02 scoping decision.

CONFIRMED recommendation (WF-03 diagnosis, 2026-07-31): (a) is already implemented and correct as a safety net but cannot fix same-invocation leaks by itself. Preferred fix is (b), scoped to the specific bare INSERT statements identified in the diagnosis report — set tenant_type='test' + production_tenant_id on each. Supplementary/defense-in-depth: add `AND tenant_type = 'production'` to GBL-084's pre-flight guard COUNT query so leaked test-typed fixtures (even before (b) fully lands, or from any future regression) cannot block the migration. A build.zig step-ordering change (clean before every individual test binary) is NOT recommended — high blast radius, reintroduces per-binary serialization cost, does not fix the underlying data-hygiene bug.

rework1_2026-07-31.trigger: TEST-RUNNER (Step 5) FAILed the shipped fix (13 files + GBL-102 guard scoping, 4 BACKEND-DEV iterations, all verified correct within their own scope): TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 (db_integration_test.zig) still fail with the exact original #357 symptom, because 15 tenant_type='production' + storage_mode='LEGACY_RLS' rows leaked by tests/integration/adp04b_tenant_realm_binding_test.zig and tm01/03/04/05_*_test.zig -- files correctly excluded from the original fix scope because they exercise the real service.createTenant() production API path, not bare fixture INSERTs.
rework1_2026-07-31.refined_root_cause_summary: NOT a declaration-order problem and NOT a panic-skips-defer bug (both ruled out with direct evidence -- see diagnosis report). The real mechanism: tests/integration/helpers.zig TestHarness.init() calls runMigrations() -> bpm.migrations.Migrations.run() UNCONDITIONALLY on every single call throughout the binary's lifetime (not once at startup), and Migrations.run() re-queries public.schema_migrations fresh every time with no in-process cache. Because GBL-102's pre-flight guard never records itself as applied while ANY tenant_type='production' + storage_mode='LEGACY_RLS' row exists (per its own header comment), it is retried and can fail on EVERY TestHarness.init() call site in the ~700-test main_test.zig binary -- not just db_integration_test.zig's two tests -- for as long as adp04b/tm0x's correctly-implemented but necessarily transient service.createTenant() fixture rows are momentarily present (their defer-based cleanup is verified correct and fires at the end of their OWN test, but a concurrently-running or not-yet-reached copy of the same ~700-test suite can have a row in-flight at the exact instant a different, unrelated test's TestHarness.init() call queries tenant state). Additionally discovered: build.zig's `test-integration-env` step (env_integration_tests artifact) was believed by TEST-RUNNER to be a scoped, isolated subset -- it is not; it compiles the identical tests/integration/main_test.zig full ~700-test suite as `test-integration` does, just as a second separate binary. This is why TEST-RUNNER's 'isolated single-binary run' still reproduced the identical leak: it was never actually isolated from adp04b/tm0x.
rework1_2026-07-31.refined_recommendation: (1) No code change needed in adp04b_tenant_realm_binding_test.zig or tm01/03/04/05_*_test.zig themselves -- their defer-based cleanup is already correct and does not need tenant_type='test' normalization (that would falsify what they test). (2) PREFERRED FIX: scope GBL-102's guard to exclude tenant slugs matching the project's existing (informal but consistent) `tc-*` test-fixture naming convention, so momentarily in-flight test fixtures never trip the guard regardless of which file created them -- pair with a lint addition (tools/lint_test_isolation.py) enforcing the tc-* prefix on any test-created tenant so the exclusion stays reliable rather than tribal knowledge. (3) Optional hardening: fix the test-integration-env build.zig step-naming/scoping confusion so future isolation attempts are trustworthy. Full rationale, evidence, and rejected alternatives in docs/issue-reports/ISS-0100-rework1-diagnosis.yaml.
rework1_2026-07-31.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for rework design (Step 2, rework_count 1)
